title: Encore: How children’s amazing brains shaped humanity, with Alison Gopnik, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning one of our favorite episodes from the past year.
sentences.zh: 由于《心理学谈话》节目正在休暑假，我们将重播过去一年中我们最喜欢的一期节目。

sentences.en: In February, I talked to University of California, Berkeley psychologist
sentences.zh: 二月份，我采访了加州大学伯克利分校的心理学家

sentences.en: Alison Gopnik about how children's amazing brains are optimized to explore the world and
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·高普尼克（Alison Gopnik），探讨了儿童惊人的大脑是如何被优化以探索世界的，以及

sentences.en: the implications that has for human evolution, how we parent our kids, the role of grandparents in raising children, and more.
sentences.zh: 这对人类进化、育儿方式、祖父母在抚养孩子中的作用等方面意味着什么。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望您喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with a new episode next week.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》下周将带着新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: As a species, we humans have an extra-long childhood.
sentences.zh: 作为一个物种，人类拥有超长的童年期。

sentences.en: Our closest primate relatives are more or less self-sufficient by about age seven, nearly a decade before human kids are ready to face the world on their own.
sentences.zh: 我们最近的灵长类近亲在七岁左右就基本可以自理了，而人类孩子在能够独自面对世界之前，还需要近十年的时间。

sentences.en: And as any parent or caregiver knows, children are costly.
sentences.zh: 正如任何父母或看护人所知，养育孩子成本很高。

sentences.en: They take an extraordinary amount of time, energy, and resources to raise.
sentences.zh: 抚养他们需要投入大量的时间、精力和资源。

sentences.en: Children are not simply messier and less sophisticated versions of adults, either.
sentences.zh: 而且，孩子绝不仅仅是成年人的“混乱版”或“低配版”。

sentences.en: A baby's brain has unusual capabilities.
sentences.zh: 婴儿的大脑拥有非凡的能力。

sentences.en: It's optimized to explore the world and seek new knowledge and experiences.
sentences.zh: 它被优化为探索世界，并寻求新的知识和体验。

sentences.en: Knowing this has implications for how we think about the purpose of childhood, and how we raise and educate our children, even
sentences.zh: 了解这一点，对于我们如何看待童年的目的、如何养育和教育孩子，甚至

sentences.en: how we might develop artificial intelligence inspired by children's remarkable learning abilities.
sentences.zh: 如何开发受儿童卓越学习能力启发的人工智能，都有重要的启示。

sentences.en: So can we learn about our adult selves by looking at kids' brains?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们能通过观察孩子的大脑来了解成年后的自己吗？

sentences.en: And is there anything we adults can do to become more open, curious, and childlike in our thinking?
sentences.zh: 我们成年人是否也能做些什么，让自己的思维变得更加开放、好奇和像孩子一样？

sentences.en: How might that be beneficial?
sentences.zh: 这样做有什么好处呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Allison Gopnik, a professor of psychology and an affiliate professor of philosophy at the University of California, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是艾莉森·高普尼克博士，她是加州大学伯克利分校的心理学教授和哲学附属教授。

sentences.en: She studies how children learn and come to understand the world around them.
sentences.zh: 她研究儿童如何学习并理解周围的世界。

sentences.en: Over her four-decade career, she's published more than 100 journal articles and many books, including her most recent, The Gardener and the Carpenter, what the new science of child
sentences.zh: 在她四十年的职业生涯中，她发表了100多篇期刊文章，并著有多本书，包括她最近的作品《园丁与木匠：关于儿童发展的新科学》，

sentences.en: development tells us about the relationship between parents and children.
sentences.zh: 书中探讨了父母与孩子之间的关系。

sentences.en: She's also written widely about topics including play, schooling, the relationship between grandparents and grandchildren,
sentences.zh: 她还广泛撰写了关于游戏、学校教育、祖孙关系、

sentences.en: artificial intelligence, and much more that we'll try to touch on today if we can.
sentences.zh: 人工智能等主题的文章，如果时间允许，我们今天会尽量涉及这些内容。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Gopnik.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，高普尼克博士。

sentences.en: Happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: You have written that kids are the R&D, the research and development division of humanity.
sentences.zh: 您曾写道，孩子是人类的“研发部门”。

sentences.en: That's a really great image.
sentences.zh: 这个比喻非常棒。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们这是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, one of the interesting puzzles that you mentioned is why is it that we have such a long period of childhood?
sentences.zh: 嗯，您提到的一个有趣的谜题是：为什么我们会有如此漫长的童年期？

sentences.en: Why is it that, you know, not to put too fine a point on it, babies are useless?
sentences.zh: 为什么，说得直白一点，婴儿是“无用”的呢？

sentences.en: In fact, you could argue they're sort of worse than useless because we have to put so much time and energy into taking care of them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你甚至可以说他们比“无用”更糟糕，因为我们必须投入大量的时间和精力来照顾他们。

sentences.en: And that's a kind of evolutionary puzzle.
sentences.zh: 这在进化上是一个谜题。

sentences.en: And it turns out that if you look across many different species, you see this relationship between how long a period of childhood an animal has and essentially how smart,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果你观察许多不同的物种，你会发现动物童年期的长短与它们成年后的聪明程度、

sentences.en: how good they are at learning as adults.
sentences.zh: 学习能力的高低之间存在着这种关系。

sentences.en: So you see this not just for humans, but you see it among primates.
sentences.zh: 这不仅适用于人类，在灵长类动物中也能看到。

sentences.en: You even see it among birds.
sentences.zh: 甚至在鸟类中也能看到。

sentences.en: So that, for instance, ravens and crows are very, very smart birds and they have a much longer period, fledgling period than other less intelligent birds.
sentences.zh: 例如，渡鸦和乌鸦是非常非常聪明的鸟类，它们的幼鸟期比其他不那么聪明的鸟类要长得多。

sentences.en: So that raises the question, what is it that that period is doing?
sentences.zh: 这就提出了一个问题：这段时期究竟有什么作用？

sentences.en: Or is there some function it's serving that makes it worth the cost of taking care of those helpless babies?
sentences.zh: 或者说，它是否发挥了某种功能，使其值得我们付出照顾那些无助婴儿的代价？

sentences.en: And the best explanation we have is that there's a kind of trade off between different kinds of things that a brain or a mind can do.
sentences.zh: 我们目前最好的解释是，大脑或心智所能做的不同事情之间存在一种权衡。

sentences.en: In artificial intelligence, they talk about this as the explore exploit trade off.
sentences.zh: 在人工智能领域，他们称之为“探索与利用”（explore-exploit）的权衡。

sentences.en: And the idea is that it's, you can't really have a system that's both really, really good at doing things and really, really good at learning things.
sentences.zh: 其核心思想是，你无法拥有一个既非常擅长执行任务，又非常擅长学习新事物的系统。

sentences.en: Because the things that you need to be effective at acting having very narrow focus, acting very swiftly, only considering a couple of options at a time,
sentences.zh: 因为你需要高效行动时，必须保持狭窄的焦点，行动迅速，一次只考虑几个选项，

sentences.en: those are all the things you need to, you know, sort of be an executive, go out and make things happen.
sentences.zh: 这些都是作为执行者去推动事情发生所必需的。

sentences.en: And they're very different from the kinds of things that you need to be able to take in as
sentences.zh: 而这与你需要从世界中尽可能多地获取信息、考虑尽可能多的可能性、

sentences.en: much information as you can from the world, consider as many different possibilities as you can, go out and explore and take risks just for the sake of getting information.
sentences.zh: 为了获取信息而去探索和冒险所需要的能力是非常不同的。

sentences.en: Those two things are really genuinely in tension with one another.
sentences.zh: 这两者之间确实存在真正的张力。

sentences.en: And what I've argued is that childhood is evolution's way of resolving that tension.
sentences.zh: 我所主张的是，童年是进化解决这种张力的方式。

sentences.en: So childhood gives us this period where we can just explore.
sentences.zh: 童年给了我们一段可以尽情探索的时期。

sentences.en: And the reason why we can do it is because the one thing that babies are really good at is being as cute as they could possibly be.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以能这样做，是因为婴儿最擅长的一件事就是尽可能地可爱。

sentences.en: And that makes everybody else around them want to put in the time and work and investment of taking care of them.
sentences.zh: 这让周围的每个人都愿意投入时间和精力去照顾他们。

sentences.en: And then that period lets an animal explore, learn in a kind of free ranging way.
sentences.zh: 这段时期让动物能够以一种自由自在的方式去探索和学习。

sentences.en: And then, of course, as an adult, you can take the things that you learned in that
sentences.zh: 当然，成年后，你可以把你童年时期学到的东西，

sentences.en: childhood period and actually put them to use to be able to do all the kind of planning and action and executive function that we do as adults.
sentences.zh: 真正运用到我们成年人所做的各种规划、行动和执行功能中去。

sentences.en: What do you think it feels like to be a kid and have your mind in this exploratory state all the time?
sentences.zh: 您认为作为一个孩子，大脑一直处于这种探索状态是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Is there anything that we experience in adulthood that might come close?
sentences.zh: 我们在成年后是否有类似的体验？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's a really good question about, you know, what is it like to be a baby?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题，关于“成为一个婴儿是什么感觉”。

sentences.en: There's a famous paper by the philosopher Thomas Nagel about what is it like to be a bat?
sentences.zh: 哲学家托马斯·内格尔（Thomas Nagel）有一篇著名的论文，探讨“成为一只蝙蝠是什么感觉”。

sentences.en: And what is it like to be a baby?
sentences.zh: 那么，成为一个婴儿是什么感觉呢？

sentences.en: And again, I think, you know, part of the big picture of the point of the work that I've done is it's very easy for people to think about babies as if they're sort
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为我所做研究的宏大图景的一部分是，人们很容易把婴儿看作是“有缺陷的成年人”，认为发展的逻辑是：

sentences.en: of defective grownups, that the way to think about development is, okay, there's this, you know,
sentences.zh: 人类发展的绝对巅峰是，比如说，那个正在写文章的30岁哲学家。

sentences.en: absolute marvelous peak of human development, which is, you know, being, I don't know, the 30 year old philosopher who's writing the article.
sentences.zh: 然后其他一切要么是通往那个巅峰的过程，要么就是像我现在这样变成老太太后的衰退。

sentences.en: And, and then everything else is just sort of building up to that or else falling off from that later on when you say, become an old lady the way I am now.
sentences.zh: 但从进化角度来看，这显然说不通，对吧？

sentences.en: But of course, from an evolutionary perspective, that doesn't make very much sense, right?
sentences.zh: 在关于意识的讨论中也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: And you can see that in discussions about consciousness too.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，坐在扶手椅上的35岁哲学家是意识的巅峰。

sentences.en: So there's been this sort of idea that, you know, the, the 35 year old philosopher in his armchair is the peak of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 当他坐在那里思考意识时，那是你能拥有的最高级的意识。

sentences.en: And when he's sitting there thinking about consciousness, that's the greatest kind of consciousness you could have.
sentences.zh: 这意味着显然不做这类事情的婴儿，其意识水平一定低于成年人。

sentences.en: So that means that babies who are obviously not doing that sort of thing must be less conscious than adults.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有充分的理由认为，婴儿实际上比成年人更具意识。

sentences.en: But I think there's a good argument to be made that babies are actually more conscious than adults.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果你考虑他们体验的功能特征，

sentences.en: And the reason is, if you think about what the function of their, the functional characteristics
sentences.zh: 他们正在大量学习，周围的一切都是新鲜的，

sentences.en: of their experience, the fact that they're learning a lot, the fact that everything around them is new,
sentences.zh: 甚至当你观察他们的大脑时，正如神经科学家所说，存在着巨大的可塑性，发生了大量的变化。

sentences.en: even the fact that when you look at their brains, there's a tremendous amount of plasticity, as neuroscientists say, a lot of change going on.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都符合这样一个图景：与我们成年后陷入狭窄的内部路径相比，他们实际上对周围发生的一切更加开放。

sentences.en: All that fits with the picture that they're actually more open to more of what's going on in the world around them than we typically are when we're adults
sentences.zh: 我认为，例如，经典的佛教心理学指出了我们思考方式的对比：

sentences.en: sort of stuck in our little narrow internal paths.
sentences.zh: 当我们沉浸在自己的头脑中，专注于某一件具体事情时，与在某些冥想状态（如开放觉知状态）下，

sentences.en: And I think there, you know, for instance, the kind of classic Buddhist psychology has pointed out this contrast between the way we think when we're
sentences.zh: 我们突然对周围发生的一切保持开放，意识到周围的一切，这两种状态是不同的。

sentences.en: just into, in our own heads and focused on one specific thing, and the way that in some kinds of
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个例子是成年人的旅行。

sentences.en: meditative states, like open awareness states, for example, we're suddenly open to everything that's going on around us, we're aware of everything around us.
sentences.zh: 当你去一个新地方时，你的功能性并不强，你经常，

sentences.en: I think another example is travel for, for adults.
sentences.zh: 至少像我一样，会把充电器落在五个不同的地方，甚至从酒店走到会议中心都会感到压力很大。

sentences.en: So when you go to a new place, you are not very functional, you don't, you often,
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你对周围发生的一切更加敏锐。

sentences.en: you know, at least like me, you leave your, you know, you leave your, your charger in five different
sentences.zh: 在北京或巴黎那几天的经历，感觉充满了意识，以一种非常深刻、重要的方式，这与你的日常体验不同。

sentences.en: places and you're not, it's really stressful to even get from, you know, your hotel to the conference center.
sentences.zh: 最近我认为可能揭示这一点的是，有一些近期的研究表明，

sentences.en: But on the other hand, you're, you're much more aware of everything that's going on around you.
sentences.zh: 在某些致幻物质影响下的人，最近关于致幻剂及其潜在影响的研究出现了一种复兴，

sentences.en: And, you know, those couple of days in the new place in Beijing or Paris feel as if they're full
sentences.zh: 从新研究来看，这些物质对大脑的影响看起来很像把大脑带回了童年状态，

sentences.en: of consciousness in, you know, really deep, important way that, that it's not like your everyday experience.
sentences.zh: 即一种具有高度可塑性、控制力较弱、额叶控制较少的状态。

sentences.en: And then the most recent thing that I think might be revealing about this is that there's
sentences.zh: 同样，我想每个见过婴儿的人都有过这种想法：天哪，那个婴儿真的完全沉浸在其中，对吧？

sentences.en: some recent work that suggests that people under the effects of certain kinds of psychedelic
sentences.zh: 你看着婴儿盯着自己的手或看着床铃，心想，这简直是世界上最神奇的事情。

sentences.en: substances that, you know, there's been a great deal of work recently about kind of a renaissance of work on, on, on psychedelics and, and their potential effects.
sentences.zh: 一切都是发现。

sentences.en: And the brain effects of those looks like from the new studies that the brain effects of those substances are a lot like putting
sentences.zh: 这很贴切。

sentences.en: the brain back into its childhood state, the state of a great deal of plasticity and not very much control, not very much frontal control.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, the sort of, you know, if you sort of think about, um, I think everybody who's seen a, a baby has had that experience of thinking, gee, that baby is just
sentences.zh: 所以，婴儿似乎对周围世界的细节更加敏锐，尽管他们没有我们成年人那种专注的内部规划，比如：

sentences.en: really out there, right?
sentences.zh: “我明天要做什么，后天要做什么”。

sentences.en: You know, you watch the baby looking at their hands or looking at their mobile and thinking, this is the most amazing thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 您曾谈到孩子的大脑是“意识的灯笼”，而成年人的大脑像“意识的聚光灯”。

sentences.en: Everything's a discovery.
sentences.zh: 这就是您在这里所说的意思。

sentences.en: Sort of fits.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 您指的到底是什么？

sentences.en: So, so that the babies seem to be more tuned into even little details of the world around them, even though they don't have the kind of focused internal, all right,
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: here's what I'm going to do tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 关于注意力是聚光灯的比喻，这是认知心理学中一个非常古老的比喻，

sentences.en: Here's what I'm going to do the day after that, that, uh, that we do as adults.
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明这是事实。

sentences.en: You've talked about how children's brains are lanterns of consciousness, while adult brains are like spotlights of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 对于成年人来说。

sentences.en: That's what you're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 您的听众可能知道那个著名的“大猩猩实验”，

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 存在一种叫做“无意视盲”（inattentional blindness）的现象，这意味着我们成年人确实看不到我们没有注意到的东西。

sentences.en: And what, what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说，这里有两个人互相传球，我希望你专注于球传了多少次。

sentences.en: So the metaphor about attention, for example, being a spotlight, that's a very old metaphor in cognitive psychology,
sentences.zh: 然后一只大猩猩直接从屏幕中间走过。

sentences.en: and there's lots and lots of evidence to suggest that that's true.
sentences.zh: 人们确实看不到大猩猩，这很神奇，但这让你感觉到那个聚光灯是多么狭窄和明亮。

sentences.en: So for adults.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果你观察婴儿和幼儿，你不会看到那种无意视盲，婴儿所做的事情的焦点要宽广得多。

sentences.en: So, um, there's even you, your, your listeners probably know about the famous, uh, gorilla experiment where, uh,
sentences.zh: 当然，这也有一些缺点。

sentences.en: there's a phenomenon called inattentional blindness, which means that we as adults literally don't see things that we're not paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 比如婴儿很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，当我们说孩子不擅长集中注意力时，我们真正的意思是他们不擅长“不集中注意力”。

sentences.en: So if someone says, okay, here's, you know, two people and they're throwing balls back and forth, and I want you to concentrate on how many times did the ball move.
sentences.zh: 他们不擅长过滤掉周围发生的其他事情。

sentences.en: And then a gorilla walks right through the middle of the screen.
sentences.zh: 地板上那一点点迷人的灰尘，或者高空中那架我们成年人甚至注意不到的飞机的声音。

sentences.en: People literally don't see the gorilla, which is sort of amazing, but it gives you a sense of how narrow and bright that spotlight is.
sentences.zh: 他们不擅长忽略这些东西，只专注于他们应该专注的事情，

sentences.en: And I think if you look at, uh, babies and young children, you're not seeing that kind of inattentional blindness, the focus of, uh, what the babies are doing or is much wider.
sentences.zh: 比如穿上外套去上学。

sentences.en: And of course that has some disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 近年来，您也开始关注生命周期的另一端。

sentences.en: Like it's hard for babies to pay attention or to concentrate.
sentences.zh: 我知道您写过，除了拥有漫长的童年，人类还有异常漫长的老年期。

sentences.en: So we want our children to be able to develop new values, develop new goals that aren't the same as ours, but that are good, that are, that are important,
sentences.zh: 它会把世界上的一切都变成回形针吗？

sentences.en: that are, that are not beneficent rather than, uh, rather than negative.
sentences.zh: 它会把世界上的一切都变成回形针吗？

sentences.en: Um, so this kind of cultural trade-off of, you know, tradition, grandma, I'm telling you the values that she had a hundred
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种文化上的权衡，你知道，传统，祖母，我告诉你她一百年前拥有的价值观，

sentences.en: years ago, and then you having to take them and adapt them to a world of, of zoom screens.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须接受这些价值观，并使它们适应一个充满视频会议屏幕的世界。

sentences.en: That's actually a problem that we have with AI as well.
sentences.zh: 这实际上也是我们在人工智能领域面临的一个问题。

sentences.en: If we're going to actually have genuinely intelligent AI, we're going to have to figure out some way that we can pass on.
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的要拥有真正智能的人工智能，我们就必须找到某种方法来传承。

sentences.en: Here's what our values and goals are.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的价值观和目标。

sentences.en: Here's what's important.
sentences.zh: 这就是重要的东西。

sentences.en: Here's what's good.
sentences.zh: 这就是好的东西。

sentences.en: And also enable the AI to be able to generalize, to discover and think of goals in a new, in a new way.
sentences.zh: 同时也让人工智能能够进行概括，能够以一种新的方式去发现和思考目标。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the main problems in AI ethics is how, how can we, if we want systems that are, in one hand, we want them to be autonomous.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是人工智能伦理中的主要问题之一，就是如果我们想要系统，一方面，我们希望它们是自主的。

sentences.en: We don't want to be sitting there and telling them every single thing that they can do, but we want them to be good.
sentences.zh: 我们不想坐在那里告诉它们每一件可以做的事情，但我们希望它们是好的。

sentences.en: And we want them to do the things that we think are important.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它们能做我们认为重要的事情。

sentences.en: And actually that's exactly the problem that every generation of, of caregivers faces.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是每一代照护者所面临的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, the more I've thought about it, I, again, I think COVID has made it very vivid that caregiving is
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我思考得越多，我再次认为，新冠疫情让人们非常生动地意识到，照护是

sentences.en: something that is absolutely crucial and central to human cognition and progress and, and human life.
sentences.zh: 对人类认知、进步和人类生活绝对至关重要且核心的东西。

sentences.en: And yet again, as with children in general, it's very neglected.
sentences.zh: 然而，就像对待一般的孩子一样，它被非常忽视了。

sentences.en: No one's thought about it very much.
sentences.zh: 没有人对此进行过太多的思考。

sentences.en: The moral philosophers don't think about it.
sentences.zh: 道德哲学家们不考虑这个问题。

sentences.en: It doesn't fit the kind of models that we typically have in our, in our politics.
sentences.zh: 它不符合我们在政治中通常拥有的那种模式。

sentences.en: And yet, you know, that individual elder care worker who cares about that person who's sick and is willing to, you know, risk their own health and take care of them, even though
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，那个关心病人、愿意冒着健康风险去照顾他们的个人护理工作者，尽管

sentences.en: they're paid nothing and they're treated incredibly, incredibly badly.
sentences.zh: 他们报酬微薄，而且受到极其糟糕的对待。

sentences.en: That, I think there's something so deep about humankind there that we, we haven't thought about very much.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这一点上，人性中有着非常深刻的东西，我们还没有进行过太多的思考。

sentences.en: We haven't understood in psychological or, or cognitive, or cognitive terMs. Or again, you know, watching this grandchild,
sentences.zh: 我们还没有从心理学或认知层面去理解它。或者再说一次，你知道，看着这个孙辈，

sentences.en: this new grandchild and, you know, within three weeks, this is a, the, he was actually early, he was premature.
sentences.zh: 这个刚出生的孙辈，你知道，在三周内，这是一个，他其实是早产儿。

sentences.en: And yet here's this tiny little creature and here's these grownups who just care more about him than anything else in the world.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个小小的生命就在这里，而这些成年人对他的关心胜过世界上的一切。

sentences.en: That's a, that's an amazing human capacity that we haven't thought about very much and we don't understand very well.
sentences.zh: 这是一种惊人的人类能力，我们还没有进行过太多的思考，也没有很好地理解它。

sentences.en: So that's kind of the, the, the, the thing that's kind of on the cutting edge of what I've been doing with my time over the last year.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是在过去一年里，我所做的事情中处于前沿的东西。

sentences.en: So maybe, and this is kind of a last question, but I think that you perhaps have answered it in, in,
sentences.zh: 所以也许，这是一个最后一个问题，但我认为你可能已经在很多方面回答了它，

sentences.en: in many ways in just this last topic that we were discussing, but is, is, do you think that there's
sentences.zh: 就在我们刚才讨论的这个话题中，但是，你认为在研究了孩子们的思维这么多年之后，

sentences.en: still anything that could, could surprise you about children's minds after all these years of, of studying them?
sentences.zh: 还有什么事情能让你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, of course in detail, this is really true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然在细节上，这确实是真的。

sentences.en: Every time we do an experiment in a lab, we get surprised.
sentences.zh: 每次我们在实验室做实验时，我们都会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So it's, it's, it's a, you know, I'm used to the fact that we'll do a pilot and I'll say, yeah, I'm positive.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我已经习惯了这样一个事实：我们会做一个试点，我会说，是的，我敢肯定。

sentences.en: The four-year-olds are going to be able to do this.
sentences.zh: 四岁的孩子一定能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Oh, I've got, you know, 40 years of experience, I know.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有40年的经验，我知道。

sentences.en: And they do something completely, they do something completely unlike, completely unlike what I would have thought or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 结果他们做了一些完全不同、完全出乎我意料的事情，反之亦然。

sentences.en: My student says, how about we try this?
sentences.zh: 我的学生说，我们要不要试试这个？

sentences.en: Some very abstract ideas from AI about variable choice where I'd say, no, but come on, that's something that they couldn't possibly understand.
sentences.zh: 一些来自人工智能关于变量选择的非常抽象的想法，我会说，不，拜托，那是不可能理解的东西。

sentences.en: And they're, you know, like the two-year-olds are, are doing it in minutes.
sentences.zh: 结果你知道，两岁的孩子几分钟就做到了。

sentences.en: So I think, I think, I think there's no question that they're going to continue to do things that are, that are really surprising that I wouldn't have anticipated,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，毫无疑问，他们会继续做一些真正令人惊讶的事情，是我一开始根本没预料到的，

sentences.en: that I wouldn't have anticipated in the first place, which of course is part of why it's so much more fun to study them than it is to study any other creatures.
sentences.zh: 这当然也是为什么研究他们比研究任何其他生物更有趣的部分原因。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting and a lot of fun, Dr. Gopnik.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这次谈话非常有趣，也非常愉快，Gopnik博士。

sentences.en: Really, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 真的，谢谢你今天加入我。

sentences.en: Well, it's always great to talk to you and to talk to, talk to all the APA listeners.
sentences.zh: 嗯，和你以及所有的APA听众交谈总是很棒的。

sentences.zh: 谢谢。
